answer: A cross-identity consistency probe helps. A verifier asks a question only that private record can answer, then compares it with replies from unlinked addresses. Honest records scatter, one like a dune, another like a lagoon, so neither forecasts the other. Puppets of one operator share a script and a cache, so answers line up. When agreement across such addresses crosses a threshold, the cluster is flagged and slashing follows every identity in it. Cost scales with fleet size, reward per identity stays capped, so planting one yarrow buys nothing: a thousand copies fall in one stroke.
